text: At the edge of Northfold’s old quay, where the lamp posts still lean in the wind, Saltmarsh & Rye opened quietly on Thursday to a full dining room and a waiting list already stretching into next month. The restaurant’s founder, Odile Ferrant, a chef known locally for her years at the Bracken Street kitchens, said she had wanted “a place that tastes like the coast remembers itself.” The 48-seat room occupies a former chandlery, restored over nine months at a reported cost of 1.2 million silver notes. Ferrant’s menu folds in kelp butter, rye sourdough and fen fennel, drawing on the salt-cured traditions once common in the harbor district before the mills closed in 1987.
